faq: Will the discounts hurt my profit margin?
We set each offer against your product costs, which you share with us, and keep the saving small enough that the order still pays. You approve every discount before it is switched on.
Do I need an app for bundles?
Often one is useful, though some platforms have built-in discounts that do the job. We choose the lightest option and tell you the monthly cost before installing.
Can offers appear only for some shoppers?
Yes, where your tools allow. For example, show a bundle only on a certain collection, or a gift only above a set cart value. We explain the limits of your plan first.
Do the offers work with my inventory?
Yes. We check that bundled items track stock correctly, so you do not oversell an item that is also sold alone.

desc:
Bundles, upsells and cross-sells setup helps shoppers find useful extras and raises order value without pressure. Ecom Swift LLC plans the offers around your products and margins, builds them in your own store and tests each one with a real order.

## Why offers need a plan

Selling more to the same visitor is often easier than finding a new visitor. A shopper who already trusts you and has a product in the cart is open to a sensible extra. But offers work only when they fit. A random product suggested next to a phone case feels like noise, while a screen protector feels like help.

Offers also carry risk. A discount set too deep can turn a sale into a loss, and an offer that conflicts with another discount can confuse the checkout. Planning before building protects your margins and your customers' patience.

## What is the difference between a bundle, an upsell and a cross-sell?

A bundle groups several products at a combined price. An upsell encourages a shopper to choose a better or larger version of the item they are viewing. A cross-sell suggests a related item that goes with what is already in the cart, such as a case with a phone or a conditioner with a shampoo.

Each fits a different moment. Bundles suit the product page, cross-sells suit the product page and cart, and a post-purchase offer suits the confirmation step.

## How offers change order value

The mechanism is simple: the shopper has already decided to buy, so adding one more useful item takes little extra effort. A clearly priced bundle also makes the saving easy to see, which removes the need to work out whether buying several items together is worthwhile.

Tiered offers, such as buying more to save more, give a concrete reason to add a second or third item. A free gift above a set spend works in a similar way. All of these depend on your products, audience and margins, so we describe the setup, not the result.

## What a good offer setup includes

- Offers chosen from your best sellers and typical order contents.
- Bundles with a clear saving shown on the product page.
- Related products placed where shoppers are already looking.
- Buy more, save more tiers with thresholds you can afford.
- A cart add-on that can be added in one tap.
- A free gift rule above a chosen spend, where it suits your margins.
- A post-purchase offer shown after payment, where your platform supports it.
- Discount rules checked against your costs and shipping.
- Stock and variant handling, so offers never sell what you do not have.
- Offer wording that explains the value in plain terms.

## How we set it up

We begin by looking at your catalog and orders to see what is often bought together and which products have room for a discount. Then we propose offers and agree on the details with you. We set them up in your own store using built-in features or a suitable app, whichever fits your platform and budget.

Each offer is tested with a real order to confirm the price, the discount, the tax and the stock behavior. We also check how the offer looks on mobile and desktop, and write the wording so it is short and honest.

The Basic package sets up one bundle and related products on your product pages, with a margin check and a test order. The Standard package adds more bundles, tiered offers, cross-sell pairings and a cart add-on. The Premium package extends to more bundles and pairings, a post-purchase offer, a free gift rule and an offer performance view in analytics. Add-ons include an extra bundle, a post-purchase upsell or a set of offer banners.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Offer items that genuinely go together.
- Check every discount against your profit on that product.
- Show the saving clearly in dollars or in plain words.
- Test the offer with a real order, including shipping and tax.
- Review what sells after a few weeks and adjust.

**Avoid:**
- Stacking several discounts that fight each other.
- Pushing expensive add-ons next to a low priced item.
- Showing too many suggestions at once.
- Offering bundles that include slow selling stock only.
- Using pressure wording that makes shoppers feel rushed.

## Who this is for

This service suits a store with many one-item orders that wants to raise order value gently, a seller whose products naturally work in sets, and an owner who tried a bundle app but was never sure the discounts were safe for margins.

## What we need from you

Send a list of your best sellers, your cost or lowest acceptable margin for each, and any products you want paired. Please give us collaborator, staff or developer access to your store, and keep your password to yourself. Your order is followed by a short checklist of what to send.
